name: Premium 5/8" Crane Sling Kit
title: Premium 5/8 Crane Sling Kit for Tree Removal
meta: A premium 5/8 crane sling kit puts a matched set of rope chokers on the truck for crane-assisted tree removal. What it is for, how to use it, how to inspect it.
tagline: A matched set of 5/8 in rope chokers for crews doing crane removals.
summary: A premium 5/8 crane sling kit bundles several 5/8 in rope crane slings so a crew has chokers ready for every pick. Rope slings are lighter to climb with than chain or wire and easier on the climber's hands, which matters when you are setting picks all day.
highlights: Several 5/8 in premium rope crane slings in one kit
Eyes at both ends for choker hitches
Lighter to carry aloft than chain or wire rope
Lets the climber pre-set the next pick
Rated slings: check each tag before use

body.h: Why buy crane slings as a kit
p: On a crane job the climber rarely uses just one sling. While one piece is in the air, the next choker is already going on, and a third may be waiting on a stem that needs two slings to balance. Buying 5/8 in premium crane slings as a kit means every sling on the truck matches in diameter and construction, so the crane operator and climber know what they are working with on every pick.

The 5/8 in size suits the bulk of residential crane removals: big enough for heavy wood, light enough that a climber can carry several on the saddle. Check the listing for the lengths included. Single slings are in our crane slings section.

Crane work is no place to guess. The weight of every pick must stay within the working load limit marked on the sling, allowing for the choker hitch and the sling angle, and the crane operator should know the estimated weight before the cut. Use crane slings only on crane picks and only as the tag and the crane company's lift plan allow.

Inspect every sling before each job. Retire any sling with cut or abraded strands, glazing, chemical damage, a missing or unreadable tag, or damage at the eyes. Store the kit clean and dry, out of the sun and away from saw fuel. Everyone involved should be trained in crane-assisted tree work and ANSI Z133 requirements.

faq.q: What length crane slings come in the kit?
faq.a: Kits are usually built around common choker lengths. Check the product listing for the exact count and lengths before ordering.

faq.q: Can I use crane slings for regular rigging?
faq.a: Keep crane slings for crane picks. Shock loads from conventional rigging are a different job, and mixing uses makes it harder to track sling condition.

name: DMM Keanu Pip Pin
title: DMM Keanu Pip Pin: Spare Pin for the Keanu
meta: The DMM Keanu pip pin is a spare locking pin for DMM's Keanu trolley. Why to carry a spare, how to check it, and why only the genuine DMM pin should be used.
tagline: A spare DMM pip pin for the Keanu trolley, so one lost pin does not end the job.
summary: The DMM Keanu pip pin is the spare locking pin for DMM's Keanu trolley pulley. Pip pins are small and easy to drop out of the tree, and a trolley without its pin is a trolley you cannot use.
highlights: Genuine DMM spare for the Keanu
Keeps the trolley usable if a pin is lost
Small enough to live in the gear bag
Check fit and function before loading

body.h: Why carry a spare pip pin
p: The Keanu is built to ride a tensioned line, and the pip pin is part of what lets you load it onto the line and close it securely. Pins get dropped in leaf litter, left in a pocket, or bent when the trolley is thrown in the truck. A spare in the gear bag costs little and keeps a speedline job moving.
Use only the DMM pin made for the Keanu. A pin from another device may look similar but differ in diameter, length or locking action. Other small hardware is in our rings and other hardware section.

Before each use, confirm the pin goes fully home, the locking balls engage, and it cannot be pulled out without pressing the button. Replace a pin that is bent, sticky, corroded, or slow to lock. Keep it clean of sap and grit, which can stop the balls seating.

Speedlining and other tensioned-line work put real loads on hardware. Follow DMM's instructions for the Keanu and ANSI Z133, and make sure the crew is trained in tensioned-line rigging before using it.

faq.q: Will this pin fit other DMM pulleys?
faq.a: It is sold for the Keanu. Do not assume it fits other devices; check DMM's information for any other use.

faq.q: Can I use a hardware-store pip pin instead?
faq.a: No. Use the genuine DMM part so dimensions and locking action match what the device was designed and tested with.

name: CMI Neptune Rigging Hub
title: CMI Neptune Rigging Hub: Multi-Point Anchor Hub
meta: The CMI Neptune rigging hub gives several connectors their own place at one anchor. What a rigging hub does, where it helps in tree work, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A multi-point hub from CMI for tidy anchors with several connectors.
summary: The CMI Neptune rigging hub is a multi-point connector that gives carabiners, pulleys and slings their own attachment points at a single anchor. It keeps a busy anchor organized so each piece loads in line instead of crowding onto one carabiner.
highlights: Multiple attachment points at one anchor
Keeps connectors from cross-loading each other
Useful for redirects, haul systems and rescue setups
Made by CMI, a rope rescue hardware maker
Check the marked rating before use

body.h: What a rigging hub does on a tree job
p: When three or four connectors end up on one carabiner, they twist, load across each other and become hard to unclip. A hub like the Neptune spreads them out. One point goes to the anchor sling, and the others take a pulley, a haul system, a lanyard or a backup, each hanging in its own line of pull.
Climbers use hubs at a rescue or haul anchor, and ground crews use them to keep a mechanical advantage system tidy. Compare other options in our rings and other hardware section.

Read the ratings marked on the hub and in CMI's instructions, and keep every load within them. Load the hub through its intended points, keep connectors seated where they belong, and avoid levering a carabiner across an edge of the hub.

Inspect before each use for cracks, deep gouges, sharp edges, deformation and corrosion. Retire a hub that has been dropped from height onto a hard surface if you have any doubt. When it is part of a life-support or rescue system, it must meet ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, and the people using it should be trained.

faq.q: Is a rigging hub the same as a rigging plate?
faq.a: They do the same basic job of spreading connectors at one anchor. Hubs and plates differ in shape and hole layout, so pick the one that fits your setup and ratings.

faq.q: Can I use it for climbing?
faq.a: Only where CMI's instructions allow it and the setup meets ANSI Z133. Check the markings and documentation first.

name: CMI Throw Line Cube
title: CMI Throw Line Cube: Collapsible Throw Line Storage
meta: The CMI throw line cube is a collapsible box for stuffing and throwing line without tangles. How a cube speeds up line setting and how to pack it for clean throws.
tagline: A collapsible cube that keeps throw line ready to fly and folds flat in the truck.
summary: The CMI throw line cube is a collapsible fabric container that stands open on the ground so you can stuff throw line in and throw again without tangles. It folds flat for storage, which helps when gear space on the truck is tight.
highlights: Stands open on the ground for quick stuffing
Lets line pay out cleanly on the next throw
Folds flat for storage
Holds throw line and a weight between jobs

p: Setting a climbing line usually takes more than one throw. With a cube, the line goes straight back into the box after a miss, and the next throw pays out from the top without the snarls you get from a pile on the grass. That saves real time on a tall tree with a tight target crotch.
Stuff the line in loosely rather than coiling it, and keep the end tied off or clipped to the cube so you do not throw the whole line into the tree. See other options in gear storage.

body.h: Living with it on the job
p: Set the cube on level ground clear of brush and sticks that can snag the line as it pays out. When the job is done, stuff the line back in with the weight on top, fold the cube down and keep it with the climbing kit so the next setup starts clean.
Keep throw line out of saw fuel and bar oil, and wash out grit and leaves now and then. Dirty line is harder to throw and wears faster.

faq.q: Will a cube hold more than one throw line?
faq.a: Many climbers keep two lines in one cube, often in different colors. Keep them separate if you want them to stay tangle-free.

faq.q: Do I need a cube or will a bag do?
faq.a: A bag works, but a cube that stands open is quicker to stuff and throw from, which is why most climbers prefer one.

name: Hard Body Spiked Felling Wedge
title: Hard Body Spiked Felling Wedge for Back Cuts
meta: A hard body spiked felling wedge has gripping spikes that help it bite and stay put in the back cut. How to use it for lifting, and when to retire a plastic wedge.
tagline: A hard plastic felling wedge with spikes that help it stay put in the kerf.
summary: A hard body spiked felling wedge is a plastic felling wedge with spikes or barbs on its faces that grip the wood so it is less likely to back out of the cut. The hard body takes heavy blows from an axe or sledge without mushrooming as fast as softer wedges.
highlights: Spiked faces help the wedge grip the kerf
Hard body takes heavy driving
Plastic, so it will not damage a chain on contact
Use for lifting and keeping the back cut open
Cheap enough to keep several on the saw belt

p: Smooth plastic wedges can spit back out of a wet or frozen kerf, especially when you drive them hard or the tree settles. Spikes on the faces give the wedge some bite, so it stays where you set it while you drive it home or step around the stump.

Set the wedge in the back cut as soon as there is room, then drive it to keep the kerf open and lift the tree toward the face. Use plastic or composite wedges near a running chain, never steel. More options are in felling wedges.

Stack wedges or use two side by side for more lift, and keep a few sizes on the belt. A wedge is not a substitute for a good face, proper hinge and correct back cut. Felling should follow ANSI Z133 and be done by trained sawyers with proper PPE.
Retire wedges with cracked bodies, deep cuts from the chain, or heads so mushroomed that they glance off when struck. A broken wedge in a loaded back cut is the last thing you want.

faq.q: Do spikes make a wedge harder to remove?
faq.a: A little, which is the point. Tap it from the side or drive a second wedge if you need to pull one.

faq.q: Can I drive it with a steel sledge?
faq.a: Yes, that is what a hard body wedge is for, but expect the head to wear over time and replace it when it starts to fail.

name: Arborwear Tech Double Thick Pullover Sweatshirt (Navy/Orange)
title: Arborwear Tech Double Thick Pullover, Navy/Orange
h1: Arborwear Tech Double Thick Pullover Sweatshirt, Navy/Orange
meta: The Arborwear Tech Double Thick pullover in navy and orange is a two-layer work sweatshirt for cold mornings in the tree. Fit, warmth, and how it handles sweat.
tagline: A heavy two-layer work sweatshirt in navy with orange, built for tree crews.
summary: The Arborwear Tech Double Thick pullover is a heavyweight two-layer work sweatshirt in a technical fabric, here in navy with orange. It is the layer for cold mornings that you can keep on while climbing and dragging brush.
highlights: Two-layer construction for warmth
Technical fabric that handles sweat
Navy body with orange accents
Pullover style, nothing to snag
Made for working, not lounging

body.h: A sweatshirt built for the job
p: Ordinary hoodies stretch out at the cuffs and soak through on the first climb. The Tech Double Thick takes Arborwear's double-layer idea and builds it in a technical fabric, so it stays warm when the morning is cold and dries better once you start working hard.
The navy body hides sap and bar oil, and the orange gives a bit of contrast against the canopy. A pullover has no zipper to catch on a lanyard or saddle. See the rest of our sweatshirts and jackets.
Size it to wear over a T-shirt or base layer and under a shell when it rains. Check that the length stays tucked under your saddle without riding up when you reach overhead.

Wash it cold, keep it away from saw fuel, and hang or tumble low to keep the fabric in shape. A sweatshirt is not high-visibility apparel; if your job requires hi-vis, wear a compliant vest or shirt over it.

faq.q: How is the Tech version different from the regular Double Thick?
faq.a: It uses a technical fabric meant to manage sweat better, while keeping the two-layer warmth of the original.

faq.q: Does it count as hi-vis clothing?
faq.a: No. Wear compliant high-visibility gear over it where roadside or jobsite rules require it.

name: CAMP Turbofoot Spare Webbing
title: CAMP Turbofoot Spare Webbing: Replacement Strap
meta: CAMP Turbofoot spare webbing replaces the worn boot strap on your Turbofoot foot ascender. When to swap it, how to fit it, and what else to check while you are at it.
tagline: Replacement strap webbing to keep a CAMP Turbofoot foot ascender in service.
summary: CAMP Turbofoot spare webbing is the replacement boot strap for CAMP's Turbofoot foot ascender. The webbing wears faster than the metal body, and a fresh strap brings back a secure fit on the boot.
highlights: Factory replacement strap for the Turbofoot
Restores a snug fit on the boot
Cheaper than replacing the ascender
Swap it at the first sign of fraying

p: A foot ascender lives on your boot. The webbing grinds against bark, gravel and spur straps, takes every step of a rope walk, and soaks up sap and mud. Long before the cam and body are worn out, the strap starts to fray, stretch and slip, and a foot ascender that shifts on your boot makes every step sloppier.
Spare webbing lets you refresh the fit without retiring a good ascender. Make sure it matches your Turbofoot version. Other foot gear is in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Thread the new webbing exactly as CAMP's instructions show, then test the fit on your climbing boot before going up. The ascender should sit firmly and not twist when you step.

While the strap is off, inspect the cam teeth, spring and pivot, and look for cracks or heavy wear on the body. Clean sap and grit out of the cam. A foot ascender is part of your SRT ascent system: follow the maker's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be trained in the system you climb.

faq.q: Does it fit the Turbofoot Evo?
faq.a: Check CAMP's parts information for your exact model before ordering, since straps can differ between versions.

faq.q: How often should I replace the webbing?
faq.a: Whenever it is frayed, cut, stiff with sap or no longer holds firmly on the boot.

name: Weaver Synthetic Upper Climber Straps
title: Weaver Synthetic Upper Climber Straps for Spurs
meta: Weaver synthetic upper climber straps replace worn calf straps on tree spurs. Why synthetic beats leather in the wet, how to fit them, and what to inspect on your spurs.
tagline: Replacement synthetic calf straps that hold spurs firm in wet weather.
summary: Weaver synthetic upper climber straps replace the calf straps on your climbing spurs with a synthetic material that does not soak up water or stretch like old leather. Fresh uppers keep the shank tight to your leg so the gaff goes in at a consistent angle.
highlights: Upper (calf) straps for climbing spurs
Synthetic material handles rain and sweat
Resists stretching better than worn leather
Brings back a firm fit on the leg
Pair with lower straps for a full refresh

p: The upper strap holds the top of the spur shank against your calf. When it stretches or loosens, the spur rocks on your leg, the gaff angle changes with every step, and your ankles do more work than they should. On a long removal that is tiring and makes cutting out more likely.

Synthetic straps shrug off rain and sweat and do not need the oiling leather does. Combine them with new lower straps to make an older set of spurs feel solid again. Browse spurs and parts in climbing spurs.

Check that the straps suit your spur model and your pads, then fit them so the shank sits snug without cutting off circulation. Buckles should close fully and the free ends should be secured so they do not catch on brush.

Inspect straps, buckles, pads, shanks and gaffs before every climb. Spurs are life-support gear on a removal: follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, use them only on removals or where rescue requires, and be trained before you climb on spurs.

faq.q: Will these fit non-Weaver spurs?
faq.a: Many spur straps are interchangeable, but check strap width and buckle style against your spurs before ordering.

faq.q: Synthetic or leather straps?
faq.a: Synthetic holds up better in wet weather and needs less care. Some climbers still prefer how leather breaks in; both work when fitted correctly.

name: 2" Bronze Swivel Snap
title: 2 Inch Bronze Swivel Snap for Gear and Tool Lines
meta: A 2 inch bronze swivel snap for tool tethers, throw line bags and gear lines. Why bronze resists corrosion, where it helps on a tree job, and what it is not for.
tagline: A small bronze swivel snap for gear lines and tethers, never for life support.
summary: A 2 inch bronze swivel snap is a small snap hook with a swivel eye, made from corrosion-resistant bronze. Tree crews use it on tool tethers, throw line bags and gear lines where a swivel keeps things from twisting.
highlights: About 2 in overall size
Bronze resists rust and corrosion
Swivel eye stops line twist
Handy for tethers, bags and gear lines
Not for life support or rigging loads

body.h: Where a small swivel snap earns its keep
p: Little snaps solve a lot of small problems on a tree job. Clip one on the end of a throw line to attach a weight or a bag, put one on a hand saw tether, or use one to hang a water bottle or radio from a saddle gear loop. The swivel lets the item spin without putting twists in the cord.
Bronze does not rust like plated steel, so it keeps working after a season of rain and sap. Larger load-rated snaps are in snap hooks.

This is a gear snap, not a connector for people or rigging. Never use it in a climbing system, lanyard, or anything that holds a climber or a load of wood. Life-support connectors must be rated and meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's requirements.
Check the gate spring now and then. A snap that no longer closes on its own should be replaced before it drops a tool out of the tree.

faq.q: Can I use it on a throw line?
faq.a: Yes, a small swivel snap is a common way to attach a throw weight or bag. Do not use it to haul a climbing line under load.

faq.q: Is bronze stronger than steel?
faq.a: No. Bronze is chosen for corrosion resistance. This snap is for light gear only.

name: 9/16" Husky Bull Rope Rigging Rope
title: 9/16 Husky Bull Rope: Double Braid Rigging Line
meta: 9/16 Husky Bull Rope is a double braid rigging line for lowering wood on removals. Where the 9/16 size fits between 1/2 and 5/8, and how to inspect and retire it.
tagline: A 9/16 in double braid lowering line between the light 1/2 and the heavier 5/8.
summary: 9/16 Husky Bull Rope is a double braid arborist rigging line for lowering limbs and wood, in a size that sits between the common 1/2 in and 5/8 in lines. It gives more strength than a 1/2 in line while staying lighter to carry and handle than 5/8 in.
highlights: Double braid rigging rope
9/16 in diameter, about 14 mm
Runs well through blocks and lowering devices
A middle size for mixed pruning and removal work
Rigging only, not for climbing

p: Many crews carry a 1/2 in line for light rigging and a 5/8 in line for the heavy stuff. The 9/16 in size splits the difference. It handles larger limbs and moderate wood with more margin than 1/2 in, but it is lighter to drag up the tree, easier on the hands and fits a wider range of blocks than the bigger line.
The double braid has a firm cover that holds up to wraps on a lowering device and runs smoothly through rigging blocks. Compare sizes in rigging rope.

Rig within the rope's working load, not its breaking strength, and remember that dynamic loads from dropping wood can multiply the force on the line, block and anchor. Match blocks, slings and lowering devices to the 9/16 in diameter and to the loads you plan to rig.

Inspect the rope before every job. Look for cuts, glazing, crushed sections, pulled strands and cover damage, and retire it if anything is doubtful. Keep it out of saw fuel and bar oil and store it clean and dry. Rigging rope is never a climbing line, and rigging should be planned by trained crew following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I use 9/16 Husky Bull Rope for climbing?
faq.a: No. It is a rigging line. Use a rope made and rated for climbing.

faq.q: Will it fit my rigging blocks?
faq.a: Check the rope diameter range marked on the block or in its instructions before using it.

name: Teufelberger 8mm Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
title: Teufelberger 8mm Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
meta: The Teufelberger 8mm sewn eye-to-eye prusik is a ready-made hitch cord for friction hitches on arborist climbing lines. Fit, rope pairing, and inspection advice.
tagline: A slim, ready-made hitch cord with sewn eyes for responsive friction hitches.
summary: The Teufelberger 8mm sewn eye-to-eye prusik is a ready-made hitch cord with a sewn eye at each end, built for tying friction hitches on your climbing line. The slim 8 mm diameter grabs firmly and tends smoothly on many common arborist ropes.
highlights: 8 mm hitch cord
Sewn eye at each end
Compact terminations keep the hitch short
Ready to tie out of the bag
Pairs with many 11 to 13 mm climbing lines

p: Hitch cord diameter sets how a hitch grips. An 8 mm cord bites harder than a 10 mm cord on the same rope, so it suits climbers on slimmer lines or anyone who wants a hitch that grabs quickly. Sewn eyes are compact compared with knotted ends, which keeps the hitch short and closer to your hand.
How it behaves depends on your rope, hitch and climbing weight, so test it low before trusting it. Other cords are in eye-to-eye prusiks.

Tie a hitch you have been trained on, dress it neatly, and test it close to the ground before climbing. If it slips or binds, adjust wraps and braids. Pair it with a micro pulley to tend the hitch smoothly.

Friction hitches build heat, so watch for glazing, stiffness and fuzzing, and replace the cord at the first sign of damage or wear in the sewn eyes. A hitch cord is life-support gear: follow Teufelberger's instructions and ANSI Z133 and inspect it before every climb.

faq.q: What rope does an 8mm prusik suit?
faq.a: It is commonly used on 11 to 13 mm climbing lines. Always test the combination before climbing on it.

faq.q: When should I retire the prusik?
faq.a: When you see glazing, cuts, stiffness, flat spots or wear at the sewn eyes, or if it fails inspection for any reason.

name: Twist-Lock Modified D Steel Carabiner
title: Twist-Lock Modified D Steel Carabiner for Tree Work
meta: A twist-lock modified D steel carabiner pairs tough steel with an auto-locking gate. Where steel beats aluminum in tree work and how to inspect a locking carabiner.
tagline: A durable steel modified D with an auto-locking twist gate for hard-wearing jobs.
summary: A twist-lock modified D steel carabiner is a hard-wearing connector with a self-closing, twist-locking gate and an asymmetric D shape. Steel holds up to rope wear and rough handling better than aluminum, which suits rigging and ground work.
highlights: Steel body for wear resistance
Modified D shape keeps loads near the spine
Twist-lock gate locks on its own
Good for rigging, haul systems and anchors
Check markings for ratings

p: Aluminum carabiners are light, which is why climbers like them on the saddle. Steel is heavier but far more resistant to grooving from rope, and it shrugs off being dropped, dragged and thrown in the truck. That makes a steel modified D a good fit for rigging points, lowering devices, haul systems and anchors.
The modified D keeps the load toward the strong spine while opening wide enough for rope eyes and slings. More auto-lockers are in auto-locking carabiners.

A twist-lock gate should snap shut and lock on its own every time. Check it before every use, and keep sap and grit out of the sleeve. Load the carabiner along its spine, avoid cross-loading and three-way loading, and keep it away from edges that can lever the gate.

Retire a carabiner with a sticky gate, cracks, deep grooves, sharp edges or corrosion. Only use it for life support if it is marked and rated for that and meets ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Is steel stronger than aluminum?
faq.a: Steel carabiners often have higher strength ratings and wear better, but they weigh more. Always read the marked ratings.

faq.q: Can I climb on it?
faq.a: Only if it is marked and certified for life support and suits your system. Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers.

name: Petzl Avao Fast Harness (International Version)
title: Petzl Avao Fast Harness, International Version
meta: The Petzl Avao Fast international version is a full-body fall arrest and work positioning harness. What international means, who it suits, and how to check it.
tagline: A full-body work-at-height harness with FAST buckles, international certification.
summary: The Petzl Avao Fast international version is a full-body harness for fall arrest, work positioning and suspension, with FAST automatic buckles that make it quick to put on. The international version is built to the certifications used outside North America, so check that it suits your jurisdiction.
highlights: Full-body harness for work at height
FAST automatic buckles for quick on and off
Fall arrest and work positioning attachment points
International version, separate from the North American model
Suits bucket, utility and rope access work

body.h: Where it fits in tree work
p: Tree climbers usually work from a saddle, but a full-body harness comes into play in aerial lifts, on utility jobs, for rope access and anywhere fall arrest is required. The Avao Fast gives fall arrest attachment points along with positioning and suspension, and the FAST buckles let you get in and out without rethreading.

Petzl sells the Avao in different versions for different markets. The international version carries the certifications used outside North America, which may not be what your employer or local rules require. Compare options in fall protection.

Size the harness to your body and work clothing, adjust it fully, and hang test it before work. Use the attachment points only for the purposes Petzl specifies, and pair it with connectors and lanyards suited to fall arrest.

Inspect webbing, stitching, buckles and attachment points before each use and keep a record. Retire it after a fall arrest or when inspection finds damage. Fall protection must follow the manufacturer's instructions and the rules for your work, including ANSI Z133 for tree work, and users must be trained.

faq.q: What is the difference between the international and North American versions?
faq.a: They are built to different certification schemes. Choose the version that matches the standards required where you work.

faq.q: Can I use it as a tree climbing saddle?
faq.a: It is a work-at-height harness rather than a dedicated arborist saddle. For routine climbing, most arborists use a tree climbing saddle.

name: Petzl Sequoia Replacement Bridge (2019 Updated Version)
title: Petzl Sequoia Replacement Bridge, 2019 Version
h1: Petzl Sequoia Replacement Bridge (2019 Updated Version)
meta: The Petzl Sequoia replacement bridge, 2019 updated version, swaps out a worn bridge on Sequoia saddles. How to check fit, when to replace it, and how to inspect.
tagline: The updated replacement bridge for Petzl Sequoia saddles, the part that wears first.
summary: The Petzl Sequoia replacement bridge, 2019 updated version, is the replacement bridge for Petzl Sequoia tree climbing saddles. The bridge takes rope wear from your hitch and hardware every day, so replacing it on schedule keeps the saddle in service.
highlights: Replacement bridge for Petzl Sequoia saddles
2019 updated version
Cheaper than replacing the saddle
Install and check per Petzl's instructions
Inspect before every climb

p: The bridge is where your climbing system attaches, and everything slides along it all day. Carabiners, rings and hitch climbers grind at the rope, and sap, grit and heat speed up the wear. That is why a bridge is meant to be replaced long before the rest of the saddle.

Petzl updated the Sequoia bridge in 2019. Check which saddle and bridge you have before ordering so the new part matches your saddle's attachment points. Other parts are in saddle parts and shoulder harnesses.

Follow Petzl's instructions for swapping the bridge, including how it is routed through the saddle's attachment points and how any connectors are closed. Have a competent person check it if you are unsure, and hang test before climbing.

Inspect the bridge before every climb for cuts, glazing, flat spots, core damage and wear at the ends. Retire it at the first doubt. A bridge is life-support gear and must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's requirements.

faq.q: Will the 2019 bridge fit an older Sequoia?
faq.a: Check Petzl's compatibility information for your saddle's model and year before ordering.

faq.q: How often should I replace the bridge?
faq.a: Whenever inspection shows wear or damage. Heavy climbers often go through bridges in a season or less.

name: 5/8" Whoopie Ring Sling with Large Ring
title: 5/8 Whoopie Ring Sling with Large Ring
h1: 5/8" Whoopie Ring Sling with Large Ring
meta: A 5/8 whoopie ring sling with a large ring gives you an adjustable rigging point and a smooth ring for natural-crotch style lowering. Uses, setup and inspection.
tagline: An adjustable 5/8 in sling with a large ring for a smooth, quick rigging point.
summary: A 5/8 whoopie ring sling with a large ring combines an adjustable whoopie sling with a large rigging ring on the fixed eye. It gives you a low-friction point to run a rigging line through, set at the right spot on stems of many sizes.
highlights: 5/8 in adjustable whoopie body
Large ring for a smooth rope path
Fits stems from small to large
Fast to set, no knots
Ratings on sling tag and ring markings
specs: See sling tag and ring markings

body.h: How a ring sling is used
p: A ring sling gives you a rigging point that works like a natural crotch but with less wear on the tree and the rope. Run the rigging line through the ring, choke or girth the sling on the stem and snug it up with the adjustable eye. The whoopie body means one sling suits a wide range of stem sizes.
The large ring gives the rope room and a smooth bend. Some climbers pair two ring slings to create a friction point or a redirect. More adjustable slings are in adjustable slings.

A ring adds friction compared with a block, which helps on some lowering jobs but also means more heat and wear. Keep loads within the lowest rating in the system, including the sling, ring, rope and anchor, and allow for shock loading.

Inspect the sling before every job for cut or pulled strands, glazing, crushed sections and splice damage, and check the ring for grooves, cracks or sharp edges. Retire anything doubtful. Rigging should be planned by a trained crew following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I use a ring sling in place of a block?
faq.a: For lighter pieces and certain techniques, yes. Heavier rigging generally calls for a block, which reduces friction and wear.

faq.q: How do I adjust a whoopie sling?
faq.a: Pull the tail to shorten the adjustable eye until it is snug. Follow the maker's instructions for minimum bury and tail length.

name: Mastodon 5/8 in. 12-Strand Rigging Rope
title: Mastodon 5/8 Rigging Rope, 12-Strand
meta: Mastodon 5/8 rigging rope is a 12-strand braided lowering line for removals and heavier wood. Why single braid is easy to splice and inspect, and how to rig with it.
tagline: A 5/8 in 12-strand lowering line for removals, easy to splice and inspect.
summary: Mastodon 5/8 rigging rope is a 12-strand single-braid line for lowering heavier limbs and wood on removals. The 5/8 in size steps up from the 1/2 in version for bigger pieces, and the 12-strand braid is simple to inspect and splice.
highlights: 5/8 in diameter
12-strand single braid
Easy to inspect and splice
For lowering heavier wood on removals
Rigging only, not for climbing

p: The 1/2 in Mastodon line handles everyday pruning cuts and small wood. When the removals get bigger, the 5/8 in version adds strength and a thicker line that is easier to grip and wrap on a lowering device. It is a good main lowering line for crews who regularly take down large trees.

Single-braid construction shows its damage on the outside, so you can see cuts and pulled strands during inspection. It also takes a spliced eye quickly with a fid. Compare other lines in rigging rope.

Match the rope to blocks, rings and lowering devices that accept 5/8 in line. Rig within the working load, and allow for shock loads from dropping pieces, which can be several times the weight of the wood.

Inspect before every job and retire the rope if you find cuts, heavy fuzzing, glazing, stiff or crushed sections or chemical damage. Keep it away from saw fuel and bar oil. This is a rigging line, not a climbing rope, and rigging should be done by trained crews following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I climb on Mastodon rigging rope?
faq.a: No. Use a rope made and rated for climbing.

faq.q: Why choose 12-strand over double braid?
faq.a: 12-strand is simple to splice and inspect. Double braid has a protective cover and different handling. Both are common rigging choices.

name: Winch Line for Stein SS RC Winch
title: Winch Line for Stein SS RC Winch
h1: Winch Line for Stein SS RC Winch
meta: A replacement winch line for the Stein SS RC winch, for pulling over trees and tensioning lines. How to match the rope to your winch and inspect it before each pull.
tagline: Replacement rope for the Stein SS RC winch, sized to the drum and the job.
summary: This winch line for the Stein SS RC winch is a replacement rope for Stein's portable winch, used to pull over trees, tension lines and move heavy wood. A rope matched to the winch runs properly on the drum and keeps the system working as designed.
highlights: Replacement line for the Stein SS RC winch
Matched to the winch's rope requirements
For pulls, tensioning and directional felling assistance
Inspect before every pull

p: A portable winch is only as good as the rope on it. Diameter, construction and stretch affect how the line grips and stores on the drum, and a mismatched rope can slip, wear quickly or overload the winch. Ordering the line made for the SS RC winch takes the guesswork out of it.

Crews use a winch to pull trees over against a lean, tension a speedline, or skid logs where a vehicle cannot reach. Check the winch manual for rope type and diameter before ordering. Related gear is in mechanical advantage.

Before each pull, inspect the rope for cuts, abrasion, glazing, crushed sections and splice damage, and retire it if in doubt. Anchor the winch to something that will not move, and keep the crew out of the line of fire and the bight of the rope.
Winching puts high, steady loads on rope, slings and anchors. Know the ratings of every component, follow Stein's instructions and ANSI Z133, and make sure operators are trained.

faq.q: Will this rope fit other capstan winches?
faq.a: It is offered for the Stein SS RC winch. Check another winch's manual for its rope requirements before using it there.

faq.q: How long does winch rope last?
faq.a: It depends on loads and use. Retire it when inspection shows wear or damage, not on a fixed schedule.

name: Edelrid Talon Lower Straps
title: Edelrid Talon Lower Straps: Replacement Ankle Straps
meta: Edelrid Talon lower straps replace worn ankle straps on Edelrid Talon climbing spurs. When to swap them, how to fit them, and what else to inspect on your spurs.
tagline: Factory replacement ankle straps for Edelrid Talon climbing spurs.
summary: Edelrid Talon lower straps are the replacement ankle straps for Edelrid Talon climbing spurs. They hold the foot stirrup firmly to your boot, so fresh straps keep the spur from rolling under your instep.
highlights: Made for Edelrid Talon spurs
Holds the stirrup tight to the boot
Replaces frayed or stretched straps
Pair with the upper strap system for a full refresh

p: The lower strap is what keeps the spur locked to your boot. When it stretches or frays, the stirrup shifts and the spur can roll, which changes the gaff angle and puts strain on your ankle. On a long removal that shows up as fatigue and a less secure stance.

Lower straps get hammered by bark, brush and boot laces, so they often wear out before the uppers. Replacing them is cheap compared with new spurs. More Talon parts, including gaffs and upper straps, are in replacement gaffs and parts.
Install the straps following Edelrid's instructions and check they hold the stirrup firmly to your boot without pinching. Secure loose ends so they cannot catch on brush or the other spur.
Inspect straps, buckles, shanks and gaffs before every climb. Spurs are life-support gear on a removal: follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be trained before you climb on them.

faq.q: Do these fit other spurs?
faq.a: They are made for Edelrid Talons. Check width and attachment before trying them on other spurs.

faq.q: Should I replace uppers and lowers together?
faq.a: If both are worn, yes. Otherwise replace whichever fails inspection.

name: ISC Captive Eye Supersafe Carabiner
title: ISC Captive Eye Supersafe Carabiner
meta: The ISC captive eye Supersafe carabiner holds a rope eye or sling in place with a captive eye and locks with ISC's Supersafe gate. How it is used and how to inspect it.
tagline: An auto-locking carabiner with a captive eye that holds terminations in position.
summary: The ISC captive eye Supersafe carabiner is an auto-locking connector with a captive eye at one end that keeps a rope eye, sling or device in position. The Supersafe gate locks automatically, and the captive eye stops the carabiner from rotating into a cross-loaded position.
highlights: Captive eye holds terminations in place
Prevents rotation and cross-loading
Supersafe auto-locking gate
Popular for lanyards and termination points
Made by ISC

p: A normal carabiner can turn under load so the rope eye slides toward the gate or the minor axis. A captive eye traps the termination in the correct position, so the carabiner stays oriented along its spine. That makes it a good choice at the end of a lanyard, on a rope termination, or on a device where you want a clean, consistent clip.
The Supersafe gate locks on its own when you let it close, which removes one more thing to think about aloft. Other auto-lockers are in auto-locking carabiners.

Confirm the gate closes and locks fully on its own and that the captive eye holds the termination as intended. Keep sap and grit out of the gate and sleeve. Retire the carabiner if it is cracked, deeply grooved, bent or has a sticky gate.
Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I remove the captive eye?
faq.a: Follow ISC's instructions. The eye is meant to be installed with a termination in place; do not modify it.

faq.q: Is it suitable for a flipline?
faq.a: Captive eye carabiners are commonly used at lanyard ends. Check that it suits your lanyard's termination and ISC's guidance.

name: 7/8" Whoopie Sling
title: 7/8 Whoopie Sling for Heavy Rigging
meta: A 7/8 whoopie sling is an adjustable rigging sling for heavy blocks and big wood. Why go up to 7/8 in, how to set it on large stems, and how to inspect it after use.
tagline: A heavy-duty adjustable sling for big blocks, big stems and heavy removals.
summary: A 7/8 whoopie sling is an adjustable arborist rigging sling sized for heavy removals and large rigging blocks. Like smaller whoopies, it has a fixed eye and an adjustable eye, so one sling fits stems of many sizes, with the extra strength that big wood calls for.
highlights: 7/8 in hollow-braid body
Fixed eye and adjustable eye
Sized for heavy blocks and big stems
Adjusts to fit, no knots needed
Ratings on the sling tag

p: Most crews start with 1/2 in and 5/8 in whoopies, which cover everyday rigging. When you are hanging a large block for heavy wood or rigging big leaders on a removal, a 7/8 in whoopie gives a stronger sling that matches heavier blocks and rope.

The adjustable eye lets you choke a large stem and pull the sling tight without tying a knot, then loosen it easily after the job. It is heavier than smaller slings, so it is a removal tool rather than an everyday pruning sling. Compare sizes in adjustable slings.

Keep the rigging load within the sling's working load limit, allowing for the hitch, the sling angle and shock loading. Every piece in the system, including block, rope and anchor, needs to be sized for the same loads.

Inspect before every job for cut or pulled strands, glazing, crushed sections and damage near the splices and at the adjustable eye. Retire it if anything looks wrong. Heavy rigging should be planned by a trained crew following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is a 7/8 whoopie overkill for pruning?
faq.a: Usually. A 1/2 or 5/8 in sling is lighter and handles typical pruning loads. Save the 7/8 for heavy removal rigging.

faq.q: How do I loosen a whoopie after a heavy load?
faq.a: Push slack back toward the adjustable eye by working the braid. Do not cut or pry at it.

name: Bulk Webbing by the Foot
title: Bulk Webbing by the Foot for Tree Work
meta: Bulk webbing by the foot lets you cut exactly the length you need for gear loops, tethers and tie-downs. Where cut webbing fits in tree work and where it does not.
tagline: Webbing sold by the foot for gear loops, tethers and other non-life-support jobs.
summary: Bulk webbing by the foot is flat synthetic webbing sold in whatever length you need. Tree crews use it to make gear loops, tool tethers, bag straps and tie-downs, buying only as much as the job requires.
highlights: Sold by the foot, cut to length
Flat synthetic webbing
Handy for gear loops, tethers and tie-downs
Seal cut ends to stop fraying
Homemade webbing items are not for life support

body.h: Uses around the truck and the tree
p: A few feet of webbing solves a lot of small jobs. Tie a loop to hang a hand saw on the saddle, make a handle for a rope bag, strap a gas can in the truck bed, or wrap a branch to keep a throw line from sawing into bark. Buying by the foot means you get the exact length and keep the rest on the roll.
Heat-seal the cut ends with a lighter or hot knife so they do not unravel. Other small gear is in other climbing gear.

Knotted or homemade webbing should not be part of any climbing or rigging system that holds a person or a load of wood. Life-support slings and lanyards must be manufactured, rated and certified, and must meet ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.
Keep webbing away from saw fuel and sharp edges, and replace it when it shows cuts, fraying or sun fading. It is cheap, so there is no reason to keep using worn pieces.

faq.q: Can I make my own friction saver from webbing?
faq.a: No. Use a manufactured, rated friction saver for anything in your climbing system.

faq.q: How do I stop the ends fraying?
faq.a: Melt the cut ends carefully with a flame or hot knife until the fibers fuse.

name: Reecoil Full Reach Chainsaw Lanyard
title: Reecoil Full Reach Chainsaw Lanyard
meta: The Reecoil Full Reach chainsaw lanyard is a retractable saw tether with extra reach for long cuts aloft. How it differs from shorter lanyards and how to set it up.
tagline: A retractable saw tether with extra reach for climbers making long cuts aloft.
summary: The Reecoil Full Reach chainsaw lanyard is a retractable tether that connects a saw to your saddle and gives extra reach for long cuts. It stretches when you reach out and pulls the saw back toward your hip when you let go, instead of leaving it swinging below you.
highlights: Retractable design pulls the saw back to the hip
Extra reach for long cuts
Keeps the saw from hanging low
Connects saw to saddle
Reecoil design built for tree climbers
specs: Tethering a saw to a climbing saddle

p: A short lanyard can stop you before the bar reaches the cut, especially when you are working out on a limb or bucking a big leader. A lanyard with full reach lets you extend the saw to arm's length, and the retracting action brings it back close when you are done instead of letting it dangle by your knees.
Climbers who carry larger saws or work long laterals tend to like the extra length. Compare other tethers in chainsaw lanyards.

Attach the lanyard to a saddle point meant for a saw, never to your climbing bridge or life-support attachment. Connect the saw end to the saw's lanyard ring, and check that the lanyard cannot drag the saw into your climbing line or legs.

Inspect for cuts, frayed webbing, stretched or damaged retracting cord, and worn connectors before each climb. Saw lanyards are not life support, but they keep a running saw controlled near you. Work aloft with a saw only if you are trained and follow ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I use it with a rear-handle saw?
faq.a: Saw lanyards are mainly used with top-handle saws aloft. Follow the saw and lanyard makers' guidance.

faq.q: Does it replace a bungee lanyard?
faq.a: Yes, it does the same job but retracts more cleanly, so the saw rides closer to your hip.

name: ART SpiderJack 3
title: ART SpiderJack 3: MRS Mechanical Friction Device
meta: The ART SpiderJack 3 is a mechanical friction device that replaces a friction hitch on a moving rope system. How it climbs, tends and descends, and what to inspect.
tagline: ART's third-generation mechanical hitch for MRS climbers who want smooth tending.
summary: The ART SpiderJack 3 is a mechanical friction device that takes the place of a friction hitch on a moving rope system (MRS). It is the third generation of ART's SpiderJack, built for smooth tending as you climb and controlled descent when you work your way down.
highlights: Mechanical replacement for a friction hitch
Built for MRS (moving rope) climbing
Self-tends as you climb
Smooth, controlled descent
Replacement parts available

body.h: Why climbers switch to a mechanical hitch
p: A friction hitch needs constant attention: dressing, setting, adjusting for wet rope and replacing cord as it glazes. A mechanical device like the SpiderJack 3 gives a consistent grip and release from day to day, tends smoothly with a pulley, and stays the same through a long day of work positioning.

The SpiderJack line has been around for years, and the third generation builds on earlier models such as the 2.1. Read ART's rope compatibility guidance before choosing a line. Compare devices in devices for MRS.

Mechanical devices behave differently from hitches. Learn the SpiderJack 3 low and slow with someone experienced, and follow ART's instructions for setup and rope range. Do not climb on it until you can operate it without thinking.

Inspect before every climb for worn friction surfaces, cracks, bent parts and damage to any textile components, and replace wear parts as ART specifies. It is life-support gear: follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Can I use the SpiderJack 3 on SRS?
faq.a: It is designed for MRS. Check ART's instructions before using it in any other configuration.

faq.q: Are parts available?
faq.a: Yes, ART offers replacement parts for the SpiderJack 3 so worn components can be swapped.

name: Freeworker TreeAustria Pro Climbing Harness
title: TreeAustria Pro Climbing Harness by Freeworker
meta: The TreeAustria Pro climbing harness is a European-style arborist saddle with a bridge attachment and a supportive sit. Who it suits and how to fit and inspect it.
tagline: A European bridge saddle from Freeworker for long days working in the canopy.
summary: The TreeAustria Pro climbing harness is a European-style arborist saddle from Freeworker, built around a bridge attachment for free movement at the waist. It is aimed at climbers who spend long days positioned in the tree and want a supportive sit.
highlights: European-style arborist saddle
Bridge attachment for side-to-side movement
Supportive for long work positioning
Replacement bridges and parts available
From Freeworker, maker of the TreeAustria line

p: A bridge saddle lets your climbing system slide side to side as you reach and turn, so you can work around the stem without fighting the attachment point. The TreeAustria design spreads your weight across the waist belt and leg loops so you can stay in position for hours.
The Pro was part of the TreeAustria line alongside models such as the 3.2. Compare it with other European saddles in European saddles.

Try the saddle on with your work clothes and hang in it before buying if you can. Leg loops and waist belt should hold you upright and comfortable without pinching, with the bridge sitting at the right height.

Inspect the bridge, webbing, stitching, buckles and connecting hardware before each climb, and replace wear parts such as the bridge on schedule. A saddle is life-support gear: follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and retire it when inspection finds damage.

faq.q: Can I replace the bridge?
faq.a: Yes, TreeAustria bridges are replaceable. Use the part specified for your saddle model.

faq.q: Is a European saddle right for me?
faq.a: If you spend long periods positioned in the canopy and like free movement at the waist, a bridge saddle is a good fit. Try one before you commit.

name: CMI Maxi Rigging Plate
title: CMI Maxi Rigging Plate for Busy Anchors
meta: The CMI Maxi rigging plate is a large multi-hole plate that keeps carabiners, pulleys and slings organized at one anchor. Where it helps and how to inspect it.
tagline: A large multi-hole plate from CMI to organize a crowded anchor.
summary: The CMI Maxi rigging plate is a large rigging plate with multiple holes that turns a crowded anchor into an orderly one. Each carabiner, pulley or sling gets its own hole, so nothing loads across anything else.
highlights: Large plate with multiple attachment holes
Keeps connectors from crowding one carabiner
Useful for haul systems and anchors
From CMI, a rope rescue hardware maker
Check marked ratings

p: Anchors get busy fast. A haul system, a backup, a pulley and a lanyard can all want the same point. A rigging plate gives each one its own hole, keeps them hanging in line and makes it easy to unclip one without disturbing the others.

The Maxi size has more holes and room than a small plate, which suits larger systems and rescue setups. It is handy for ground anchors on mechanical advantage pulls too. Browse other gear in blocks and other hardware.
Load the plate through its main attachment point and keep the connectors in their own holes. Know the ratings marked on the plate and keep every load within the weakest link of the system.

Inspect before each use for cracks, deep gouges, sharp edges, bending and corrosion. When used in a life-support or rescue system, follow ANSI Z133 and CMI's instructions and make sure the crew is trained.

faq.q: Do I need a rigging plate?
faq.a: If you regularly hang several connectors from one anchor, a plate keeps them organized and loading properly.

faq.q: Maxi or smaller plate?
faq.a: A smaller plate is lighter for simple anchors. Choose the Maxi when you need more attachment points.
